newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC bank shares hit new high in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: BLC bank shares hit new high in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares were mixed on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday as Banque Audi fell back from Tuesday's record high and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce hit a new record for the second day running.
Solidere A and B shares both rose in heavy demand.
Banque Audi, which touched $26 on Tuesday, dropped to $25.875 while BLC jumped 37.5 cents to $19.25. Bank of Beirut, the third listed bank, was unchanged at $4.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.5 percent to 163.83. The LISPI general index rose 0.35 percent to 89.39 and the BLOM general index rose 0.94 percent to 940.03.
Market turnover was 112,202 shares for a value of $1,616,679 against 189,860 shares for a value of $1,763,174 on Tuesday.
The three banks -- Audi, BLC and BOB -- have risen 72.5 percent, 71 percent and 84 percent respectively since listing in the last few months.
All three traded in strong demand on Wednesday and brokers said they expected further rises.

"People are getting more excited about the banks' mid-year results. They see that banks are doing well and they want to get into the market," Alain Balian, deputy manager at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest, said.
Prices and turnover were expected to pick up after the results became known, he said.
Georges Abou Jaoude, head of Lebanese operations at Financial Funds Advisors, another Beirut finance house, said he expected BLC to continue rising after hitting new records on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"A further rise in BLC is justified because the stock is still trading at a discount compared to other bank shares," Abou Jaoude said.
Solidere A and B rose in heavy demand to $10.5 and $10.875 respectively from $10.375 and $10.75.
Demand for Solidere at the first fixing was 444,725 against 82,290 supply. Only 18,506 shares changed hands.

"Everybody wants to buy the stock. It is a good one and it is believed that the time has come for it to start moving up. The company's Global Depositary Receipts are trading at around $16.5 in London today," Abou Jaoude said.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.2812 on trade of 5,000 shares.
There was no trade in the other listed shares: Ciment Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
